A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rennala NIGT and Malenia NIGT study. Their main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-H are readable and can be reliably matched across additions and repagination.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H report original MuJoCo experiments measuring reward against emulated distributed computation time, including heterogeneous worker speeds and environments.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H retain these original experiments and their results in Figures 1-9. Results retained from v1 remain original empirical results of the work.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1-3 retain the same extrapolation, normalized momentum updates, gradient aggregation, and stopping rules. The policy architecture also remains unchanged. Section 7 analyzes these existing procedures under a different computation model.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Humanoid-v4, Reacher-v4, Walker2d-v4, and Hopper-v4, including the original/inverted-state Humanoid scenario in Appendix H.3. Section 7's computation dynamics are analyzed theoretically without adding evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: AFedPG and Synchronized NIGT remain the comparison methods in the corresponding Rennala and Malenia experiments throughout Figures 1-9. Newly cited related methods are not added to these comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix H retains the 10- and 100-agent homogeneous experiments, two-agent heterogeneous setup, horizons of 512 or 1024, timing schedules, hyperparameter searches, and reward-versus-time evaluation. No experimental protocol is revised.

E4.justification: The worker-count and computation/communication sensitivity experiments in Appendix H.2 and the heterogeneous-environment test in H.3 are unchanged. No ablation, robustness experiment, or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds per experiment and the same intervals described as '(20%, 80%) confidence intervals' in Appendix H. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1-9 retain identical plotted results and uncertainty bands. Section 6 and Appendix H retain the same findings about equal-speed performance, timing heterogeneity, and Malenia's heterogeneous-environment advantage; no empirical result entries change.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's fixed-time bounds and iteration-varying Rennala bound in Theorem 4.3, v2 adds Assumption 7.1 defining continuous-time computation powers and integrated gradient counts. Theorems 7.2-7.3 and proofs in Appendices E.2/E.4 establish recursive completion-time guarantees for both algorithms under this broader model, excluding communication costs. Existing convergence and lower-bound results remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.2 retain the same main contributions: Rennala and Malenia NIGT, improved computation and communication complexities, AllReduce support, heterogeneous-environment guarantees, and a lower bound. These advertised claims are not strengthened or narrowed.

C2.justification: Appendix G expands v1's general black-box-oracle qualification with specific open extensions to importance-sampling variance reduction and Hessian-aided methods requiring additional assumptions. Section 7 also explains fluctuating computation powers and disconnections while explicitly excluding communication costs from that extension.

D1.justification: Appendix H retains the same Gaussian policy, two 64-unit hidden layers, tuning grids, Python 3/PyTorch implementation, and Intel Xeon CPU emulation details. Code and data access information does not change.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fan et al. (2021), Ganesh et al. (2024), Labbi et al. (2025), Xu et al. (2020a,b), and Tyurin (2025). Targeted discussion expands coverage of importance sampling, Hessian-aided and fault-tolerant federated methods, and computation dynamics, while retaining the central positioning against AFedPG.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 7, proof subsections E.2/E.4, and a G.1 proof heading, alongside localized expansions of related work and lower-bound discussion. Affiliations, publication headers, and acknowledgements change, but most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 moves from page 4 to page 5, and appendix figures are repaginated, including Figure 8 appearing alone on v2 page 31. New theorem boxes and conference headers accompany the additions; existing tables and plots retain their display structures.

improvement.justification: Section 7 and its appendix proofs improve theoretical applicability by providing completion-time guarantees for both algorithms under continuous-time worker dynamics. The added related-work and lower-bound discussion also clarifies scope. The overall gain is limited: v1 already handled iteration-varying Rennala speeds, and the new extension excludes communication costs. The original algorithms and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
